Wazuh windows are codified at automation/wazuh/ism_retention_apply.sh:38-50 (90 d alerts, 30 d monitoring/statistics, with templates).

findings.title: OpenSearch sink drops failed batches with no dead-letter/replay path (detection now closed and live-verified)
findings.evidence: config/vector/aggregator.yaml:132-171 adds a 512 MiB disk buffer, end-to-end acknowledgements and 20 retries/1 h, but the only DLQ input is route_valid.invalid (:166-171). There is still no sink-failure journal, no reroute_dropped path and no capture for non-retriable mapping/4xx rejects, so a rejected batch is observed (bootstrap/90-alerting.sh:241-247) but not preserved. automation/validation/write_rejection_test.sh:52-60 exercises an index-read-only window, not a forced non-retriable mapping rejection.
findings.remediation: Add a durable sink-failure journal + replay (or a proxy/sidecar that captures 4xx rejects) and a forced-mapping-rejection drill proving every failed batch is captured and replayable.

findings.title: Live client-VPN enrollment credential is a single shared token with no expiry; per-device lifecycle implemented but unused
findings.evidence: automation/vpn/enroll-service.py:60-113 supports <name>:<token>[:expiry] and rejects expired bindings; automation/vpn/issue-enroll-token.sh:26-50 issues 24 h default per-device tokens and writes <name>.enroll-token. But the closure path still cannot prove the bare line is gone: automation/validation/enrollment_closure_check.sh:84-93 only compares the deployed file hash, docs/security/ENROLLMENT_CLOSURE.md:15 still describes one shared token baked into endpoint scripts, and automation/vpn/sync-levelio-scripts.sh:11 embeds the whole token file into every endpoint script (new ACM-P2-004). Impact while the bare token is live: authorize() accepts the shared token for any name not in `named` (:102-113) and existing_peer() replaces a block with the same name (:135-141,228-240), so a holder can re-enroll an unbound site/sensor name and take over its tunnel address.
findings.remediation: Fix the bulk-token substitution first; then issue per-device bindings for every active device, rotate/remove the bare line, and make enrollment_closure_check fail on a bare token or expired binding; bind tokens to device identity (not only a client-chosen name).

findings.title: Deployed enrollment service does not enforce per-device token expiry; issuance tool and deployed enforcement disagree (no deployed-artifact binding)

findings.title: Ingest contract relies on a shared secret header, not request signing or idempotency keys
findings.evidence: config/vector/aggregator.yaml:22-44 adds mutual TLS (verify_certificate: true) and keeps HTTP basic auth; config/vector/edge.yaml:241-256 uses the shared falcon-vector-edge credential and one client certificate. There is still no per-request HMAC/nonce or idempotency key (no such implementation in config/vector), so a holder can replay/inject and retries can duplicate.
findings.remediation: Add an HMAC/timestamp/nonce (or per-sensor certificate identity) and a deterministic document id/idempotency key; keep basic auth as a second factor.

findings.title: The only automated Access-posture check no longer verifies Access (external-smoke accepts any 302 from the lab vantage)

findings.title: Edge control-plane spool keeps purging ~134 MiB per 10-14 h; nothing consumes it and the purge alert cannot fire at that rate

findings.evidence: config/vector/aggregator.yaml:22-44 adds mutual TLS with verify_certificate: true and keeps basic auth; config/vector/edge.yaml:241-256 uses one shared client certificate. findings.title: Endpoint-script sync embeds the entire enrollment token file (all per-device tokens) into every device script
findings.evidence: automation/vpn/sync-levelio-scripts.sh:11 reads the whole /srv/falcon/secrets/vpn_enroll.token into ENROLL_TOKEN and :18-19 substitutes it into every installer/updater script. issue-enroll-token.sh:44,48 writes per-device lines <name>:<token>:<expiry> plus a <name>.enroll-token file. Once any per-device binding exists, every endpoint script receives all bindings (and the multi-line value can break or corrupt the sed substitution), defeating the per-device lifecycle and leaking credentials to every device.
findings.remediation: Generate each script from that device's <name>.enroll-token only (or inject the token at runtime); refuse to sync when the token file has more than the one intended line; add a two-binding test proving only the target token is embedded.

findings.title: SSO header adapter authenticates unsigned X-Authentik-*/Remote-* headers on 0.0.0.0:8090
findings.evidence: console/sso_gateway.py:166-186 accepts X-Authentik-Username/Remote-User and ...-Groups with no shared secret, mints an admin role when the group contains admins (:173), and returns the IRIS token at :184-185. The service binds 0.0.0.0:8090 (bootstrap/98-console.sh:239-240) and nftables allows 8090 from all Docker and management sources (config/nftables/falcon.nft:50); docs/runbooks/SSO.md:152-164 even documents the direct fake-header curl. A compromised container on 172.16/12 (or any management host) can use the returned X-Proxy-*/X-Falcon-* headers or the IRIS token against the app containers on the same Docker networks, bypassing Kestrel.
findings.remediation: Bind the adapter to Traefik's Docker gateway/loopback, require a Traefik-injected shared secret or mTLS, remove the Remote-* fallback, and add a negative test that a direct fake-header request is 401.

findings.title: Client VPN peer-class firewall rule is a hardcoded three-address set; dynamically enrolled clients .23-.99 reach the control plane and Wazuh proxies
findings.evidence: config/nftables/falcon.nft:33 drops only 10.99.0.20/.21/.22 on tcp 9443/15140/15141; automation/vpn/enroll-service.py:46,230-240 allocates any free address in 10.99.0.20-99, and docs/runbooks/VPN.md:16 documents that pool. A new client peer at .23+ is not dropped; syslog/NetFlow also remain open to all wg0 peers at falcon.nft:36-37.
findings.remediation: Replace the three addresses with the full client pool/subnet (or an nft set maintained by enrollment), keep site/sensor peers in a separate range, and add a negative test from a .23 peer.

findings.title: Console API still requires a Cloudflare Access JWT and grants admin to owner-IP/LAN, not the Kestrel identity used by Traefik
findings.evidence: console/auth.py:1-13,116-132 verifies Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion and otherwise grants admin for CF-Connecting-IP == owner or a direct private peer; config/traefik/dynamic.yml:137-157 now puts only kestrel-auth in front of the console (no Access JWT), and docs/runbooks/SSO.md:12 says the console is Kestrel gate-only. After the documented Access-app deletion, non-owner Kestrel users get 401 from the API, while bootstrap/98-console.sh:121-126 still tries to populate the Access AUD from the deleted app.
findings.remediation: Consume the Kestrel identity headers (signed by Traefik/adapter), remove the Access-JWT and owner-IP/LAN bypass for the public path, and add a test that a non-owner Kestrel user gets viewer access.

findings.title: Console action endpoints have no CSRF/Origin enforcement and trust an owner-IP/LAN admin identity
findings.evidence: console/api/server.py:722-756 accepts POST /console/api/v1/actions/{ack,unack,downtime-add}, parses the body and calls the root broker without checking Origin/Referer or a CSRF token; console/auth.py:126-131 treats the owner IP or a direct LAN peer as admin; console/web/app.js:258-262 sends the state-changing request. A cross-site POST from an owner browser (or a LAN client) can ack/unack/downtime checks and suppress alerts when the session cookie is sent.
findings.remediation: Require a per-session CSRF token and an Origin/Referer allowlist, enforce Content-Type: application/json, and use SameSite cookies; do not grant admin solely by source IP.

findings.title: Trusted-header SSO trusts entire Docker subnets: any frontend/backend container can self-assert Grafana/OpenSearch admin
findings.evidence: compose/central/docker-compose.yml:233 whitelists 172.30.2.0/24 for Grafana's auth proxy; config/central/opensearch-security/config.yml:77-79 and automation/wazuh/multi-node/config/wazuh_indexer/opensearch-security/config.yml:77-79 trust 172.30.1/2/4 as internal proxies. A compromised container on those shared networks (vector aggregator, ntop, etc.) can call Grafana/OSD/Wazuh with X-Falcon-User/X-Proxy-User: <admin> and X-Proxy-Roles: admin directly, bypassing Kestrel.
findings.remediation: Scope each whitelist to the Traefik container IP/network, strip client-supplied identity headers at the app ingress, and use mTLS/JWT between Traefik and the apps; separate the data-plane networks.
